PullRequest.Title: notebook: avoid quadratic carriage-return stream normalization
PullRequest.Body:

Normalizes ordinary carriage-return progress output without rescanning the entire stream repeatedly. The same **164 KB batch** drops from **1.30 seconds to 2.2 ms**, with identical output.

| Measured operation | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| 41 KB progress batch | 80.6 ms | 0.6 ms |
| 82 KB progress batch | 315.8 ms | 1.1 ms |
| 164 KB progress batch | 1,296.6 ms | 2.2 ms |

![Recorded before and after measurements for Notebook stdout - remove the 1.3-second stall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karthiknadig/vscode/8a50bfd61d53df3579025ef6b9f0e58ab1fbbd95/brief-performance-proof/notebook-proof.png)

**Proof scope:** Legacy dollar-text lines keep the old path. Component probe, not live-kernel execution. 68 notebook tests and 299,593 baseline compatibility comparisons passed. Legacy dollar-text behavior is intentionally preserved; those affected streams retain the old path and cost.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction clips (startup removed), implementation, and full validation commands</summary>

The clips below are brief measured-result excerpts. The comparison above is the primary performance proof; clip duration is not a benchmark.

Fixes a source-derived notebook stdout performance defect found by the performance swarm. No matching open issue or fix PR was found, and no new issue was filed. Related implementation history: #160946 (stream compression) and #188998 (compression-flag reporting, preserved here).

## Root cause

`NotebookCellOutputTextModel.appendData` normalizes terminal-style stdout before publishing the output change. `fixCarriageReturn` repeatedly searches and replaces against the entire accumulated string, consuming one carriage-return-bearing line at a time.

A batch of 4,000 ordinary progress records:

```text
Task 00000: running\rTask 00000: complete\n
Task 00001: running\rTask 00001: complete\n
...
```

is only **164,000 bytes**, but normalization blocks the renderer for about **1.3 seconds**. Doubling the input from 1,000 to 2,000 to 4,000 records produced roughly four times the runtime at each step.

## Change

For ordinary streams, process each logical line once. Walk its carriage-return segments backward and keep only the suffix not overwritten by a later segment. This preserves shorter overwrites without repeatedly rebuilding the whole stream.

- Preserve a pending final carriage return for the next append.
- Preserve CRLF, consecutive returns, Unicode line boundaries, UTF-16 overwrite behavior, and existing backspace processing.
- Keep output compression flags, version invalidation, and data-change events unchanged.
- Do not change notebook rendering, execution, or provider APIs.

### Explicit compatibility boundary

The old replacement-string algorithm has observable dollar-text quirks: for example, `$$\r\r` becomes `$`. This PR deliberately preserves them instead of combining a behavior change with the performance fix.

If a carriage-return-bearing line contains `$`, the existing algorithm is retained for that stream. Such inputs retain their previous complexity. Dollar text on an unaffected line does **not** disable the optimized path. The new tests cover both cases.

## Before / after

Same scenario, actual production output model inside Code OSS, exact output checks, one warm-up and five measured samples per size:

| Progress records | Appended bytes | Before median | After median |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,000 | 41,000 | 80.6 ms | 0.6 ms |
| 2,000 | 82,000 | 315.8 ms | 1.1 ms |
| 4,000 | 164,000 | **1,296.6 ms** | **2.2 ms** |

For the 164 KB case, the same **84,010 output bytes**, version, and event count are verified. The already-normalized same-output control takes 0.2-0.3 ms.

The unchanged scenario fails the 200 ms renderer budget before the fix and passes **3/3** in fresh fixed windows. The three after-run medians are **2.2, 2.3, and 2.0 ms**, with worst samples at or below 2.6 ms.

Windows 11 x64, AMD EPYC 7763 (32 logical processors), 128 GiB RAM, Node 24.20.0, Code OSS 1.141.0 Dev. Timings exclude input construction and assertions. Benchmarks were run sequentially under the shared measurement lease, without concurrent builds.

Baseline: `dcb81648f8a8f1863d2577f8fec98e805e5f95a0`. Fixed: `709ff28acde959947531c9aa8ac16ced1ba9b663`, based on `253b7648aa69de1a651a327370098f3814b8922f`. The relevant normalization and output-model code is identical between the baseline and the fix's parent.

## Regression coverage

- Existing notebook common and text-model suites: **68 tests passed**.
- New exact-output cases cover short/long overwrites, pending and consecutive returns, CRLF, backspace ordering, Unicode line separators, UTF-16 boundaries, and legacy dollar behavior.
- Every semantic case is also tested at every possible byte-buffer split, including inside UTF-8 sequences.
- Thousands of carriage-return segments on a single line preserve the uncovered suffix correctly.
- A 4,000-record append through the actual notebook text model preserves one output item, one data-change event, the output version, and invalidation of append-only history.
- An additional [compatibility checker](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/87412d0bd3c7e89f875e8aeb74f5b4fd0eb6a95c/notebook-stream-normalization/notebook-stream-compat.mjs) exhaustively compared **299,593 inputs** of length 0-6 over `a`, `b`, CR, LF, backspace, `$`, U+2028, and U+2029 against the unchanged implementation. Both output text and `didCompression` matched.

### Limits

These are production-component renderer measurements, not a live Jupyter kernel or end-to-end notebook-opening benchmark. No shipped-build comparison, macOS/Linux UI runs, full repository suite, or OOM test was performed. Dollar-bearing overwritten lines intentionally keep the legacy path; backspace normalization is unchanged.

</details>

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The old normalization loop repeatedly scanned, matched, replaced, and reallocated the entire accumulated stdout string once per carriage-return overwrite, making a multi-line progress batch scale approximately O(N*R), quadratic when record size is bounded.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Large notebook stdout progress batches can synchronously stall output updates and delay renderer/event publication; the PR's production-path regression test uses 4,000 carriage-return records, where the old algorithm performs thousands of full-stream passes.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added line-wise replace processes each logical line once, splits only carriage-return-bearing lines, and walks their segments once from right to left. For ordinary streams this changes normalization from repeated whole-stream work per overwrite to work linear in the decoded bytes and carriage-return segments, while retaining the legacy fallback only for dollar-bearing overwritten lines.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before this PR, fixCarriageReturn's while loop handled one carriage-return overwrite at a time; each iteration re-matched and replaced against the whole accumulated decoded stream. NotebookCellOutputTextModel.appendData synchronously calls optimizeOutputItems -> compressOutputItemStreams before incrementing the version or firing onDidChangeData, and the notebook text model emits the output-item event only afterward. The new 4,000-record model test demonstrates a realistic batch cardinality on this path. Thus R overwrite records in N bytes caused repeated whole-string scans and allocations on the notebook output update critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: A running notebook appends stdout/stderr progress output to an existing cell output and updates the visible renderer.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CellEditType.OutputItems reaches NotebookCellTextModel.changeOutputItems, then NotebookCellOutputTextModel.appendData synchronously merges and normalizes stream buffers before version advancement, onDidChangeData, notebook content events, and any back-layer webview update can proceed. The changed normalization is therefore on the update/render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the notebook OutputItem model-change event to the extension host through $acceptModelChanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing RPC payload per notebook content-change event, containing grouped raw output-item events; not one call per carriage-return record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same RPC was sent after normalization; the diff only changes CPU work performed before publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The synchronous model update and normalization complete before the content-change event is constructed and sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the updated rendered output to the notebook webview with _sendMessageToWebview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one showOutput message for the changed rendered output version; the version cache avoids resending an unchanged version.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same renderer message and version-cache behavior existed; the old repeated normalization delayed reaching it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A visible renderer cannot receive the updated output until synchronous normalization and model notification complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective input is the concatenated byte count for each MIME group plus the number of carriage-return segments in that group. A realistic tested batch contains 4,000 progress records in one output edit; grouping means this is one normalization per MIME, not one boundary call per record.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normalization is synchronous and serialized on the workbench event loop for each output edit. Carriage-return records inside one batch are processed by one call; no Promise concurrency, limiter, queue, or parallel fan-out is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no normalization cache. Each merged stream group is decoded and normalized when compression is needed. The renderer's version cache suppresses sending an already-published output version, but normalization occurs before that consumer check. Cold and warm normalization have the same complexity; ordinary streams are now linear, while the legacy dollar-bearing overwrite fallback remains pre-existing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the old loop performed whole-string regex scans/replacements once per overwrite, whereas the changed ordinary path makes one line-wise pass and one reverse pass over carriage-return segments.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency varies with batch shape, runtime, and notebook output size. The repeated whole-string mechanism and 4,000-record tested cardinality are established even without relying on a specific timing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression introduced. The PR removes repeated whole-stream CPU/allocation work from this synchronous critical path; the compatibility fallback preserves a pre-existing slow path only for dollar-bearing overwritten lines.

Scenarios.Scenario: The extension host applies a main-thread notebook OutputItem delta and updates extension-visible cell outputs.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MainThreadNotebookDocuments sends the existing model-change RPC; ExtHostNotebookDocument processes each raw OutputItem event, converts items, groups all text-stream items by MIME, and calls compressOutputItemStreams synchronously before extension-visible cell-change events are delivered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer the notebook content-change delta from the workbench to the extension host via $acceptModelChanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing RPC per content-change event, with output items serialized in that event; compression in the extension host does not add calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same event and payload crossed the boundary, followed by the old repeated whole-stream normalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The boundary delivers the delta; extension-host normalization must then finish before API consumers observe the cell change.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: For each OutputItem delta, cost scales with total retained stream bytes and carriage-return segments after grouping by MIME. Effective cardinality is one compression per MIME group in the affected output, regardless of how many progress records are in the batch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RPC deltas and their synchronous extension-host processing are serialized on the extension-host event loop. MIME groups are processed sequentially with forEach; there is no concurrency burst or additional scheduling introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No compression cache or negative cache is used. Existing output items are merged with the delta and normalized each time there is more than one all-stream item. Cold and warm behavior are equivalent; the new ordinary path reduces repeated work without changing invalidation or grouping.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setOutputItems directly invokes the changed helper after MIME grouping, and the before/after algorithmic difference is visible in the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension-host impact depends on output history, MIME grouping, and append frequency. No new boundary or concurrency was added, and the algorithmic reduction for ordinary streams is direct.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed helper lowers CPU and temporary-string allocation on this pre-existing synchronous IPC-consumer path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced both production callers. No diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold. The PR fixes a verified repeated-work regression in carriage-return normalization; its introducing commit was recorded separately.
